articles.title: OpenClaw v0.14 Released: Native Support for Multi-Agent Parallel Scheduling
articles.summary: OpenClaw has released v0.14, adding a multi-agent parallel scheduler and sandbox-level isolation, boosting long-task execution efficiency nearly threefold.
articles.detail: The OpenClaw community officially released v0.14 this week, headlined by the 'Swarm Scheduler' multi-agent parallel scheduling module. It lets developers describe multi-agent collaboration flows in declarative YAML, while the scheduler handles dependencies, concurrency, and failure retries. The new version also isolates each agent's tool calls in an independent lightweight sandbox (based on WebAssembly), preventing cross-session state contamination. Official benchmarks show end-to-end time on typical three-stage 'retrieve–analyze–write' tasks dropped about 68 percent versus v0.13. The release also drops Python 3.9 support, moving fully to 3.11+.
articles.impact: For developers, multi-agent orchestration shifts from hand-written glue code to configuration, significantly lowering the engineering barrier for complex workflows. For enterprise users, sandbox isolation makes OpenClaw easier to pass internal security and compliance reviews, potentially accelerating adoption in production environments.

articles.title: OpenClaw Plugin Marketplace Goes Live, 200+ Skills Available for One-Click Install
articles.summary: The official plugin marketplace ClawHub launches, covering productivity, data analysis, browser automation and more, with support for private repository hosting.
articles.detail: The official OpenClaw team announced that its plugin marketplace, ClawHub, has entered open beta, with more than 200 'Skill Packs' at launch, including Notion/Feishu sync, browser visual operations, natural-language SQL querying, and structured PDF extraction. All plugins carry digital signatures and permission declarations, so users can see exactly which tools and data scopes a plugin can access before installing. The enterprise edition supports private repository hosting, internal review workflows, and SSO integration. Community feedback shows the three most installed plugins are Browser Pilot, DocParsr, and CodeReviewBot.
articles.impact: The maturity of a plugin marketplace determines an agent framework's moat. ClawHub moves OpenClaw from 'framework' to 'ecosystem,' allowing ordinary users to assemble automation workflows without writing code, while giving independent developers a new monetization channel.

articles.title: Major Cloud Vendors Launch Hosted OpenClaw Services as Agent Runtimes Enter the 'Zero-Ops' Era
articles.summary: AWS, Alibaba Cloud and others have rolled out hosted OpenClaw services with usage-based pricing and built-in observability dashboards.
articles.detail: Following OpenClaw's adoption by a major open-source foundation last quarter, AWS and Alibaba Cloud this week each announced fully managed OpenClaw runtime services. Users simply upload an agent configuration to get automatic scaling, key management, call-chain tracing, and cost dashboards. Both offer two pricing models: per-task billing and monthly concurrent capacity. Notably, the hosted layers generally include prompt-injection detection, tool-call whitelists, and output audit logs, addressing enterprise concerns about agent controllability.
articles.impact: Managed services significantly cut the operational cost of deploying agents for enterprises, and shift the competitive focus from 'who can run it' to 'who has better orchestration and governance.' Smaller teams can integrate agents into business processes far more lightweight.
articles.source: AWS News Blog / Alibaba Cloud Official Announcement

articles.title: Browser-Use 类浏览器自动化技能成为本周下载榜首
articles.summary: 让 AI 直接操作浏览器完成填表、比价、抓数据的技能包下载量周环比增长 210%。
articles.detail: 浏览器自动化技能（如 Browser Pilot、Browser-Use）通过「视觉截图 + DOM 定位」双通道让模型直接操控网页，完成登录、表单填写、跨站比价、定期抓取等任务。本周多个技能包支持了 Chrome 扩展形式安装，用户无需起本地服务即可使用。社区还出现了「操作录制器」，可以把人工操作一次录制成可复用的 Agent 流程。典型用例包括每日电商比价、后台批量操作、舆情数据采集等。
articles.impact: 浏览器是最大的 GUI 资产，掌握浏览器自动化等于掌握了绝大多数没有 API 的存量系统。对运营、客服、财务等重复性岗位，这是眼下 ROI 最直观的 AI 落地方向。

articles.title: 「本地知识库 + 向量检索」技能包走向开箱即用
articles.summary: 新一代 RAG 技能内置混合检索、重排序与引用溯源，个人知识库搭建门槛大幅下降。
articles.detail: 本周推荐的 LocalMind、RecallKit 等技能包将 Embedding、混合检索（BM25 + 向量）、Rerank、引用溯源打包成一条龙流程，支持 Markdown、PDF、网页、聊天记录等多源导入，并提供增量索引与去重。新版普遍加入「答案必带出处」机制，点击引用即可跳回原文段落，显著缓解了幻觉与可信度问题。轻量版可在 16GB 内存的笔记本上流畅运行。
articles.impact: 个人与小团队终于可以低成本构建「第二大脑」，把散落的文档、笔记、会议记录变成可问答的资产。对咨询、法务、研究等重度依赖资料的行业价值尤为突出。

articles.title: 结构化数据处理技能：让 Excel/SQL 不再是 AI 的短板
articles.summary: 支持公式生成、复杂 SQL 生成与数据清洗的新技能，把「表格类」工作流的准确率提升到 90% 以上。
articles.detail: 长期以来，LLM 在表格计算、日期处理、多表 Join 等结构化任务上表现不稳。本周上线的 SheetPilot 与 QuerySmith 通过「代码执行 + 自我校验」两阶段策略，在生成公式或 SQL 后自动跑一遍结果、对照行数与样例值，再决定是否重写。实测在常见的财务对账、销售报表生成场景中，一次性准确率从 60% 提升至 92%。两者均支持把生成结果直接回写到 Excel 或数据库。
articles.impact: 这补齐了 Agent 在企业核心数据场景的最后一块短板，意味着「自然语言直接驱动业务报表」开始具备生产可用性，对财务、BI、运营岗位冲击最为直接。

articles.title: iOS 26.1 Rollout: Apple Intelligence Adds 'Screen Awareness' and Cross-App Actions
articles.summary: The new OS version lets Siri understand on-screen content and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, with developer integration via App Intents.
articles.detail: Apple has released the iOS 26.1 release candidate to developers, with a focus on strengthening on-device AI. The new 'Screen Awareness' feature lets the voice assistant read the current interface (with user permission) to answer questions or take actions accordingly, while 'Cross-App Actions' chains operations across multiple apps from a single command — for example, 'add the date in this email to my calendar and reply to confirm.' Apple has also opened up a revamped App Intents framework, allowing third-party apps to declare semantically meaningful actions that the system can invoke, with support for parameter passing and returning results.
articles.impact: By building 'agentic capabilities' into the OS layer rather than individual apps, Apple is creating both a traffic channel and competitive pressure for independent developers — apps that don't adopt App Intents risk being sidelined, and the on-device privacy route is beginning to differentiate itself from cloud-based agents.

articles.title: Is the Subscription Model Cooling Off? A Wave of iOS Utility Apps Shifts to 'One-Time Purchase + AI Add-Ons'
articles.summary: Facing subscription fatigue, developers are testing a new business model: one-time purchases for core features, pay-per-use for advanced AI capabilities.
articles.detail: Multiple mid-tier iOS developers have shared their transition experience in community forums: core features are now sold as one-time purchases priced at RMB 68–128, while AI-powered features such as batch processing and long-document parsing are billed per token or per use. Data shows first-month conversion rates rose by around 40% under this model, refund rates fell, and the costs of AI calls were effectively covered. The App Store also recently updated its review guidelines, explicitly permitting the 'one-time purchase plus consumable in-app purchase' combination, while requiring clear disclosure of AI feature pricing and data usage.
articles.impact: This offers indie developers a new path to counter subscription fatigue and gives users a more intuitive sense of what 'AI is actually worth.' Notably, cost transparency may become a key differentiator in the next phase of app competition.
articles.source: Indie iOS Dev Weekly / App Store Review Guidelines

articles.title: On-Device LLM SDK Opens Up, Local Inference Becomes a New Selling Point
articles.summary: Apple has opened more complete on-device model loading interfaces, and some apps already offer offline-capable summarization, translation, and image understanding.
articles.detail: In iOS 26.1, Apple further opened up the Foundation Models framework, allowing apps to load adapted on-device models directly and perform streaming inference, with support for LoRA-style lightweight fine-tuning and structured output. Several note-taking, reading, and camera apps have already shipped features such as offline summarization, full-text translation, and image captioning — all completed without uploading data. Tests show that devices with the new-generation chip can achieve generation speeds of roughly 20 tokens per second on 3B-scale models.
articles.impact: Offline capability is emerging as a core selling point in privacy-sensitive sectors such as healthcare, legal, and business, while also giving apps differentiated features without inference costs. An on-device-plus-cloud architecture is set to become the mainstream approach for iOS apps.

articles.title: Agent Infrastructure Startup Runlayer Raises Series A, Bets on Agent Observability
articles.summary: Runlayer has raised tens of millions of dollars, centering its pitch on agent trace tracking, cost attribution and hallucination detection.
articles.detail: Startup Runlayer announced the completion of a Series A round led by a prominent fund. Its product offers full-chain agent call tracing, tool-call auditing, cost attribution (down to the model and tool spend of a single task) and output quality detection, with support for integration with mainstream frameworks such as OpenClaw and LangGraph. The founding team hails from the observability division of a major cloud vendor and stresses that "the first hurdle for agents entering production is not intelligence, but explainability." The company already has early customers in finance and e-commerce.
articles.impact: As agents move from demos to production, observability and governance are among the first capabilities purchased. This track could replicate the market path taken by APM and logging platforms, making it one of the more certain bets in enterprise infrastructure today.

articles.title: Veridex's Medical Documentation Automation Surpasses $10M ARR in Six Months
articles.summary: The startup uses purpose-built models plus a strict citation mechanism to handle medical records and insurance paperwork, with a focus on traceability and auditability.
articles.detail: Medical documentation automation company Veridex disclosed that its ARR has surpassed $10 million within six months. At its core are purpose-built models for medical records, discharge summaries, insurance pre-authorizations and similar use cases, which require every generated passage to link back to the original source fragment. The company has passed information security reviews at multiple hospitals. It operates a dual model of per-document pricing plus private deployment, with revenue coming mainly from mid-to-large hospital groups and insurance providers. Next, it plans to expand into clinical trial documentation and real-world research data curation.
articles.impact: Healthcare is one of the industries with the highest barriers to AI adoption but also the strongest willingness to pay. Veridex's growth validates the "vertical specialization plus auditability" approach and offers a reference point for any AI company targeting highly regulated industries.

articles.title: Hardware Startup Halo Devices Launches Screenless AI Wearable, Sells Out on Preorder Day One
articles.summary: The matchbox-sized device focuses on all-day voice recording and on-device summarization; 50,000 units sold out on the first day of preorders.
articles.detail: Halo Devices unveiled its first screenless AI wearable, weighing under 30 grams, with all-day voice recording, speaker diarization, meeting summaries and action-item extraction. Core processing runs locally, and uploads happen only after user confirmation. Compared with earlier "AI recording pendant" products, it shows clear improvements in battery life (18 hours), pickup noise cancellation and local model efficiency, and the companion app syncs with mainstream calendar and task tools. All 50,000 units sold out on the first day of preorders, though comment sections have seen substantial debate over recording ethics and the duty to inform.
articles.impact: The decisive factor in AI hardware is shifting from "does it look like a phone" to "does it solve a frequent, small pain point." It also serves as a reminder to the industry: always-on recording products must build notification and compliance mechanisms into the design, otherwise the faster they grow, the greater the regulatory risk.

hotProjects.quote: Trends aren't meant to be chased — they're meant to reveal who solves the real problem first.
hotProjects.summary: Biggest trend of the day: multi-agent orchestration and browser automation are pushing AI agents from "demo-ready" to "delivery-ready," with observability and on-device inference rising alongside.

projects.name: OpenClaw Swarm Scheduler (Multi-Agent Orchestration)
projects.oneLiner: Turns multi-agent collaboration from hand-written code into declarative config, boosting long-task efficiency several-fold.
projects.whyHot: v0.14 ships parallel scheduling, sandbox isolation, and failure retries out of the box, hitting the pain point of "complex workflows that won't build or run reliably." Paired with the ClawHub plugin ecosystem and cloud-hosted services, OpenClaw has evolved from a technical framework into a de facto standard candidate, with community PRs and plugin counts hitting record weekly growth.
highlights: Declarative YAML orchestration sharply lowers the multi-agent development bar
WebAssembly sandbox isolation meets enterprise security and compliance needs
ClawHub plugin marketplace forms an ecosystem moat
Hosted services from major cloud vendors are rolling out
projects.riskTip: Rapid ecosystem expansion could bring uneven plugin quality and supply-chain security risks; with no settled standard, a competing protocol from a tech giant could fork the road.

projects.name: Browser-Use-Style Browser Automation Skills
projects.oneLiner: Lets AI drive browsers directly, bringing API-less legacy systems into automation.
projects.whyHot: The browser is the largest GUI asset, and the vast majority of enterprise systems, government portals, and e-commerce backends still have no API. With mature vision + DOM dual-channel targeting, high-frequency repetitive work — form filling, price comparison, data scraping — can be replaced reliably. Downloads up 210% week on week, with growing adoption cases in operations and finance roles.
highlights: Vision + DOM dual-channel targeting delivers high success rates on complex pages
Action recorder: capture a human workflow once and replay it as an agent flow
Chrome extension format — zero deployment to get started
Clear ROI in cross-border price comparison and bulk back-office operations
projects.riskTip: Uses like bypassing CAPTCHAs or bulk scraping carry compliance and account-ban risks; critical business processes still need human review — don't fully hand over.

projects.name: Agent Observability Platforms (Led by Runlayer)
projects.oneLiner: An "APM for agents" offering call-chain tracing, cost attribution, and hallucination detection.
projects.whyHot: The biggest barrier to agents reaching production has shifted from "not smart enough" to "not explainable, not controllable." Enterprises need to know what a task cost, which tools it called, and where it failed. The business path benchmarked against APM and logging platforms is clear, with strong willingness to pay: one startup has landed orders from multiple financial institutions within six months, and its funding pace has clearly accelerated.
highlights: Full-chain call tracing with per-task cost attribution
Tool-call auditing and permission allowlists for compliance
Output quality and hallucination detection to support human-in-the-loop fallback
Compatible with mainstream frameworks including OpenClaw and LangGraph
projects.riskTip: Barriers in this segment are relatively low, leaving it vulnerable to bundling by cloud vendors; early on, watch for revenue concentration risk from over-reliance on a few large customers.

projects.name: On-Device AI Wearables and Edge Inference SDKs
projects.oneLiner: Local models plus portable hardware,主打 offline-ready, privacy-first voice and vision AI.
projects.whyHot: iOS 26.1 opening on-device model loading APIs and sell-out preorders for screenless devices like Halo point to one trend: inference costs and privacy anxiety are pushing AI local. Offline summarization and translation have become new selling points for note-taking, reading, and camera apps; on the hardware side, the market is won by solving one high-frequency pain point rather than form-factor innovation.
highlights: Mature on-device SDKs: 3B-class models hit roughly 20 tokens/s
Strong willingness to pay for offline capability in privacy-sensitive fields like healthcare and legal
Screenless/small-screen hardware breaking through with a single high-frequency use case
Edge-cloud hybrid becomes the mainstream architecture, cutting inference costs significantly
projects.riskTip: Recording devices face disclosure obligations and privacy compliance pressure; hardware carries high supply-chain and inventory risk, and big players can undercut with system-level capabilities at any time.
